verifications.claim: SpaceX successfully launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying 25 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Monday, April 6, 2026, at 7:49 p.m. PDT (10:49 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'SpaceX successfully launched 25 Starlink satellites from its Falcon 9 rocket ... on Monday, April 6, 2026 ... 7:49 p.m. PT' but also 'launched 27 Starlink satellites'; R2: 'Falcon 9 launched 25 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg ... at 10:19 p.m. Monday'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly supports most details including date, time, 25 satellites (despite one mention of 27), but R2 contradicts with different time (10:19 p.m.) and lacks specific date.

verifications.claim: The launch was visible across Southern California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'visible over Southern California'; R2: 'seen across Southern California ... Social media posts from areas such as Santa Monica and Huntington Beach showed a red streak'
verifications.reasoning: Both references directly confirm visibility across Southern California.

verifications.claim: The 1st stage booster landed on a droneship in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the first stage will land on the "Of Course I Still Love You" drone ship, which will be stationed in the Pacific Ocean'; R2: 'was expected to land on a ship in the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Both describe planned landing on droneship in Pacific post-successful launch, but use future tense ('will land', 'expected') rather than confirming it 'landed'.

verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Neither reference mentions 'Starlink 17-35' or 'V2 Mini' satellites.

verifications.claim: The launch site was Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base, CA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states the exact launch site; R2 mentions Vandenberg but not SLC-4E.

verifications.claim: The 1st stage booster had tail number B1103.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Neither reference mentions booster tail number B1103.

verifications.claim: The 1st stage booster made its 10th flight.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'This is the 10th flight for the first stage booster'; R2: 'The booster involved has already flown 13 missions'
verifications.reasoning: R1 supports 10th flight, but R2 contradicts with 13 missions.

verifications.claim: The replay of the launch is available on SpaceX's X account.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Rewatch the April 6 launch'; R2: 'The launch was streamed live on SpaceX’s website and X account'
verifications.reasoning: R1 mentions rewatch (platform unspecified), R2 confirms live stream on X implying replay availability, but neither explicitly states 'replay available on X account'.

verifications.claim: The flight was previously delayed from Sunday.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The launch was originally scheduled for Sunday evening'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly confirms prior scheduling for Sunday; R2 does not mention.
